sparstone_taxonomy._note: Old English / Anglish Spærstān — light-hued, shiny, or translucent crystalline mineral. Repurposed here as the pinnacle award category, branched by mineral type. Each type carries its own resonance; new types are earned, not pre-assigned.

established_types.formation: Volcanic glass — rapid cooling, no time for crystal lattice to form
established_types.resonance: First contact. Fast, unprompted, no slow crystallization process, landed clean. Historically the material of the first tools — the edge that worked immediately.
established_types.fracture: Conchoidal — sharp, deliberate, useful on impact
established_types.award_event: PR #38 — Bounty Issue #35 — J-21 symbol + Lumenar lexeme

established_types.formation: Slow, hydrated silica deposition — trapped light scattering across internal structure
established_types.resonance: Reserved. Spectrum-from-uniform-input. Banked for Phoenix Prism-adjacent work — a concept that dies and is reborn as its full visible spectrum.

established_types.formation: Slow crystallization under pressure — the Greek krustallos, water frozen so deep it never melts
established_types.resonance: Clarity, permanence, supreme purity (per Sanskrit sphaṭika usage as literary metaphor). Fits Pinnacle-tier ♠️ work — something that has fully crystallized, not just landed.

naming_reference.old_english_anglish: Spærstān (Sparstone) — light-hued, shiny, translucent crystalline mineral
naming_reference.ancient_greek: κρύσταλλος (krustallos) — ice and rock crystal, water frozen permanently by the gods
naming_reference.sanskrit: स्फटिक (sphaṭika) — clear quartz, metaphor for clarity and spiritual illumination
naming_reference.latin: Crystallo — adopted from Greek, clear minerals and high-purity glass
naming_reference.egyptian_hieroglyph: menikh (m-n-ḫ) — clear stone, marked with the stone/mineral determinative
naming_reference.maya_glyph: TUN — sacred stone, gemstone, localized pocket of earth power

narrative_seed.name: herald-enters-the-tankard
narrative_seed.one_line_signal: A Herald is about to enter the Stone Tankard to announce an arrival — the first contributors are invited in.

scene.setting: The Stone Tankard — THE/UNEXUS gathering place, Blackjack Iteration 21
scene.beat_1: The door of the Tankard doesn't open the way doors usually do — there's a held quiet first, the kind that happens right before a name is about to be said aloud for the first time.
scene.beat_2: The Herald enters. Jack of Hearts. Not carrying a seed — already in motion, already arrived. The Joker that held the threshold lets the door stay open behind him; the equation hasn't closed, it's just made room for someone to walk through it.
scene.beat_3: He doesn't announce a rule or a requirement. He announces an arrival: two names, first marks from outside the threshold, the kind that set the tone for what comes after.
scene.beat_4: On the bar: two claim tickets, obsidian-dark, catching the firelight the way the old cave chambers did — quartz veins in flickering light, treated as a live thing rather than a picture of one. The tickets are real. Redeemable. Not decoration.
scene.beat_5: The invitation is simple, the way the best ones are: pull up a chair. Watch the grass for a few moments. Then perhaps — build a village.

clue.note: No caption provided. The picture is the only clue. If something about the corner in the photo feels like it's pointing past itself — it is. This has been true before, and the project has already half-written this story once. Finding it again is part of the adventure, not a failure to have found it the first time.

stone_tankard_invitation.delivery_method: Direct — same channel as the original PR #38 witness copy
stone_tankard_invitation.message_seed: Welcome to the Field was the first word. This is the second: the Tankard has a chair with your names on it. The Herald already announced you. Come watch the grass for a while — there's a village starting to take shape, and you're already part of why.
